title: Charge ASG extinction exponentially in selection excess over mutation
statement: ForDelta=(S-alpha0)_+,D=ceilDelta,F=(1+Delta/alpha0)4^D, the accepted lineage chainb_n=Sn/2,d_n=n(alpha0+n-1)/2 has product ratios over ANY indexinterval<=F: only factors atell=1 and at mostD laterindices exceed1,andprod_(k=1)^D(1+D/k)=binom(2D,D)<=4^D. Minimal absorptionincrements yieldDelta_n<=2F/(n-1) for n>=2,Delta_1<=F(2/alpha0+2); beyondn>2S+2 the tail improves to4/[n(n-1)]. Hence sup_n E T_n<=16BF. Markov/strong-Markov blocks give whole-row TV(O_(t,x)^r,O_infty^r)<=2^-floor(t/[32B(1+Delta/alpha0)4^D]),uniform inK,r,x including boundary. IfD<=floor(log2B),F<=B^4 andexpectedextinction<=16B^5. This sharpens the earlier e^S upper certificate without proving an exponential lower bound for actual mixing or resolving unrestricted strong excess selection.
